$$F(x^+)\le F(x)+Q_i(z_i)-Q_i(x_{B_i})+\epsilon_j.$$
Averaging over the uniform block choice at this fixed history therefore gives
$$\mathbb E[F(x^+)\mid\text{history}]\le F(x)+\frac{M_x(z)-F(x)}n+\epsilon_j.$$
All quantities are finite at these points because accepted model gaps and exact block minima are finite. [A2, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

Convex differentiability of $f$ gives $f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),w-x\rangle\le f(w)$. Indeed, apply its convex segment inequality at $x+s(w-x)$, subtract $f(x)$, divide by $s>0$ and let $s\downarrow0$. Thus, for $w_s=(1-s)x+sx^*$,
$$M_x(w_s)-F(x)\le F(w_s)-F(x)+\frac{L_{\max}s^2}2\|x^*-x\|_2^2.$$
These segment values are finite by convexity of the effective domain. Apply [A1] to obtain
$$M_x(z)-F(x)\le-s(F(x)-F(x^*))+\frac{L_{\max}s^2-\mu s(1-s)}2\|x^*-x\|_2^2.$$
Choose $s=\mu/(L_{\max}+\mu)\in(0,1)$. The squared-distance coefficient vanishes, so $M_x(z)-F(x)\le-s(F(x)-F(x^*))$. This does not require $\mu\le L_{\max}$. [A1, F9, step 1.1, step 1.2, given, algebra]

Substitute step 2.1 in step 1.2 to get
$$\mathbb E[F(x^{j+1})-F(x^*)\mid\text{history}]\le q_c(F(x^j)-F(x^*))+\epsilon_j.$$
By [A2] all histories in the finite product distribution are present; summing the inequality with their weights gives $\phi_{j+1}\le q_c\phi_j+\epsilon_j$, where $\phi_j=\mathbb E[F(x^j)-F(x^*)]$. No conditioning on the event of a successful inner solve is used. [A2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

The proposed bound at $k=0$ is $\phi_0=\phi_0$. If $\phi_j\le q_c^j\phi_0+\sum_{\ell<j}q_c^{j-1-\ell}\epsilon_\ell$, multiply by $q_c>0$ and use step 3.1 to obtain the bound at $j+1$. Finite induction proves the displayed convolution. It specializes to exact-update contraction when every $\epsilon_j=0$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, induction, algebra] ∎
